newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says in touch with overseas on forex policy.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says in touch with overseas on forex policy.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) are keeping in contact with overseas authorities for appropriate management of policy on foreign exchange rates, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsuhita told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
"In implementing policy on foreign exchange, the Finance Ministry and the Bank of Japan are keeping in contact with overseas (authorities) and working for appropriate management," Matsushita said.
He added that responsibility for stabilising currencies through intervention lies in the hands of the government, and the BOJ works as an agent of the government in carrying out intervention.
Asked if the BOJ should also pursue currency stability as a goal of its monetary policy, Matsushita said doing so could adversely affect its aim of stabilising domestic prices.

But since currency movements affect the real economy, the central bank needs to grasp the overall movement of the economy including the impact of currency rates in order to pursue continued stable growth with stable prices.
"Our policy goal is to stabilise prices including the impact of currency movements (on prices)," he said.
